commits.subject: gmp: Import `exponent` so the `BigInt` method is reachable (#63257)

review.summary: Reviewed both commits, their first-parent diffs, Joolia’s existing zero-origin adaptations, and the merged result at HEAD. No additional source or test adaptation is needed: the changed values are dispatch, mathematical exponents, counts, or already-correct zero-origin limb positions.

commits.subsystems: Base.GMP BigInt dispatch in base/gmp.jl (`GMP.exponent`, `_bit_magnitude`, `top_set_bit`); Base.Math `exponent` fallback in base/math.jl; test/intfuncs.jl allocation and BigInt exponent coverage. Base.jl loading order was inspected: Math is included before GMP.
commits.indexing_implications: The changed import at base/gmp.jl:13 makes `GMP.exponent(::BigInt)` extend `Base.exponent`, so BigInt calls reach the limb-based implementation instead of the generic Integer fallback. In base/gmp.jl:629-635, `x.size` is a signed limb count, while `x.size - 1` passed to `unsafe_load` is the zero-origin final limb position; this existing Joolia adaptation is correct and must not be changed. The returned `_bit_magnitude(x) - 1` is a mathematical binary exponent, not a collection position. `@allocated` in test/intfuncs.jl measures an allocation byte count, not an index. Callers including `top_set_bit` and base/intfuncs.jl:841 were inspected.
commits.adaptations: None. The only commit source change is the missing Base generic-function import. Joolia’s existing zero-origin limb accesses and BigInt storage contract are already present in the resulting tree; changing the import or exponent arithmetic would either leave the dispatch bug or alter a mathematical result.
commits.tests: Recommended, not executed: run the existing test/intfuncs.jl and test/gmp.jl targets in fresh Joolia processes, checking `exponent(big(2)^100 ± 1) == 99/100`, negative and zero DomainError behavior, and the existing zero-allocation assertion after compilation. Also run `make -C test base-foundation` and the required `python3 contrib/ci/run.py --jobs 4` gate. No runtime tests were run because this review has no built Joolia.

commits.subsystems: Base.Math numeric dispatch and documentation in base/math.jl (`exponent(::Integer)`, `exponent(::Base.BitInteger)`, `exponent(::Bool)`); Core/Base Bool and Integer hierarchy in base/boot.jl and base/int.jl; test/intfuncs.jl.
commits.indexing_implications: The new `exponent(::Bool)` method at base/math.jl:992-998 returns the mathematical exponent of `true` (0) and rejects `false` because it represents numeric zero. The returned 0 is a mathematical value, not a zero-origin position or sentinel. Bool is an Integer according to base/boot.jl, but is not included in the `Base.BitInteger` union defined in base/int.jl, so the exact Bool method is needed to avoid the generic `_ilog2_step` path. Existing `exponent(::Integer)` values, including its initial shift/count arguments, were classified as mathematical logarithm state and counts rather than collection indices.
commits.adaptations: None. The resulting method preserves upstream intent and is already compatible with Joolia’s zero-origin contract; no array, tuple, dimension, range, memory, compiler-ID, or foreign-ABI index is introduced. The compat documentation is version metadata, not an index.
commits.tests: Recommended, not executed: run test/intfuncs.jl in normal and minimal compilation modes and verify `@inferred(exponent(true)) === 0` plus `@test_throws DomainError exponent(false)`, alongside existing integer boundary cases. Run `make -C test base-foundation` and the required `python3 contrib/ci/run.py --jobs 4` gate. No runtime tests were run because this review has no built Joolia.
